summary: Neo enters a kitchen where an old woman is peering into an oven; she confirms she is the Oracle and, without looking, warns him not to worry about a vase—whereupon he turns and his elbow knocks a vase off a table, breaking it. She pulls out chocolate chip cookies and reveals herself as a grandmotherly figure. She deflects his question about how she knew, turning it into a riddle about whether he would have broken it anyway. She tells him being the One is like being in love, something you just know, then examines him physically and scripts the moment where he admits he is not the One. She tells him he has the gift but is 'waiting for something,' possibly his next life. When Neo laughs about Morpheus almost convincing him, she grows serious and prophesies that Morpheus will sacrifice his life to save Neo's, forcing Neo to choose which of them dies. Neo is stunned. She softens, telling him he'll feel better once outside and that he's in control of his own life, then gives him a cookie she promises will make him feel right as rain, and the tightness in his chest begins to fade.

what_changes.before: Unsure whether he is the One, telling the Oracle 'Honestly? I don't know.'
what_changes.after: Told by the Oracle that he is not the One and is instead 'waiting for something,' possibly 'Your next life, maybe.'
what_changes.evidence: ORACLE: Sorry, kid. You got the gift but looks like you're waiting for something. NEO: What?

what_changes.before: Struck breathless and terrified by the prophecy that he must choose between Morpheus's life and his own.
what_changes.after: Calm returning as he eats the cookie, 'the tightness in his chest slowly beginning to fade.'
what_changes.evidence: Neo takes a cookie, the tightness in his chest slowly beginning to fade.

what_changes.before: Playful and teasing, calling Neo 'cuter than I thought' and 'Not too bright though.'
what_changes.after: Solemn and Sphinx-like, delivering fatal news: 'One of you is going to die. Which one, will be up to you.'
what_changes.evidence: The Oracle takes a long drag, regarding Neo with the eyes of a Sphinx. ORACLE: Are you sure you want to hear this?

event_hint.one_line: Neo visits the Oracle, who tells him he is not the One and foretells that Morpheus will die to save him.

objects_that_matter: the tray of chocolate chip cookies
uncertain: Whether the Oracle's prediction about Morpheus sacrificing himself is genuine foresight or a manipulation designed to steer Neo.
Whether the cookie has any real effect or works as a placebo alongside her suggestion.

minds.wants: To get Neo to a specific inner position: to stop performing belief/disbelief for Morpheus and instead take responsibility for a choice, without her having to command it.
minds.feels: A working, almost maternal fondness for him mixed with the fatigue of someone who has delivered this same devastating news before (the 'five before me' from sc-083 hangs over her). She is not guessing at his terror—she is administering it in a measured dose, then antidoting it.
minds.shows: A flustered, teasing grandmother: cookies, oven mitts, jokes ('Not too bright though'), a wink. The warmth is partly real and partly the delivery system for the prophecy—she softens him so the blow lands where she wants and so she can walk it back on cue.
minds.basis: She predicts the vase before he turns, scripts his 'But what?' dialogue, physically examines him like a doctor, and—only after he's shattered—reassures him and hands him a cookie that she promises will fix how he feels, which it does. The warmth and the cruelty are the same hand.

believes_about.belief: That he is a 'good soul' worth protecting, fundamentally decent and frightened, not a messiah to be flattered.
believes_about.wrong_because: It is partly a strategy: treating him as an ordinary scared boy is exactly what keeps him from inflating into the One Morpheus needs, which is her aim.

believes_about.belief: That his blind faith is a liability that will get him killed for a belief she does not share.
believes_about.wrong_because: Unstated but dramatic: her prophecy about his self-sacrifice is itself the lever that will convert Neo from doubter into believer—Morpheus's 'wrong' faith becomes the instrument that makes it right.

minds.wants: To get certainty—either confirmation that he is the One, or permission to stop carrying Morpheus's certainty for him.
minds.feels: Relief and dread braided together: the verdict 'not the One' lets him set down a burden he never wanted (echoing sc-083's 'I don't believe in this stuff'), but the prophecy about Morpheus instantly replaces it with a heavier, moral one—guilt and the terror of being made responsible for another man's death.
minds.shows: A wary, slightly sarcastic visitor trying to stay cool ('Morpheus. He almost had me convinced'), then visible collapse ('can't breathe'), then a docile, nodding boy accepting comfort and a cookie as the tightness leaves his chest.
minds.basis: He hovers at the door in sc-083 refusing to believe; here he readily accepts 'I'm not the One,' almost laughs, and only loses composure when Morpheus's death is named. The cookie physically easing his chest shows how suggestible—and how soothable—he is.

believes_about.belief: That she is a benign fortune-teller reading a fixed future and then kindly softening the blow.
believes_about.wrong_because: She demonstrates control over him (the vase, the scripted lines, the mood-shifting cookie) that looks less like foresight and more like steering; whether the prophecy is fate or a push he cannot yet tell.

believes_about.belief: That her reassurance—'you're in control of your own life'—is true comfort.
believes_about.wrong_because: She has just told him the opposite: that a choice he must make will decide who dies. The comfort and the prophecy contradict, and he is too relieved to notice.

believes_about.belief: That Morpheus's certainty is a problem to be escaped, a weight Neo never asked for.
believes_about.wrong_because: He does not yet see that being the reason Morpheus would die is what will make belief impossible to avoid—his attempt to set the burden down is the first step toward taking up the real one.

connects_back: sc-083: Neo's hallway refusal to believe and Morpheus's confession about the five dead predecessors—Neo's ready acceptance of 'not the One' is him finally agreeing with his own skepticism.
sc-082: Morpheus framing the Oracle as a 'guide,' not infallible—Neo enters expecting a verdict on his identity and gets a redirection instead.
sc-084: the Potentials ('there is no spoon') priming the idea that reality bends to belief—the Oracle's vase trick is the first live demonstration Neo witnesses.
sets_up: ev-021: The instruction to keep the verdict secret from the crew begins as Neo's private, guilty knowledge.
ev-022: The 'one of you will die, and it's up to you' prophecy becomes the operative frame during the Hotel Lafayette raid and Morpheus's capture.
ev-026: Neo's insistence on rescuing Morpheus—defying Tank's 'suicide'—is the choice the Oracle said he'd have to make; her prophecy has pre-loaded his sense of responsibility.
The cookie's soothing effect establishes Neo's suggestibility, the same seam self-belief will later exploit when he stops trying and starts knowing.
dramatic_function: To convert Neo from a passive doubter into a morally responsible agent: the Oracle dismantles his borrowed identity ('not the One') only to hand him a heavier, self-authored one (the man who must choose who dies), so that the coming rescue is his free choice rather than Morpheus's prophecy fulfilled.
